name: investment_fibo
description: Investment relationship ontology — investor/manager relationships, subscription agreements, fund commitments and their commercial terms. Translated 1:1 from the owner-supplied OWL/Turtle (http://example.org/investment#, :InvestmentRelationshipOntology) 2026-08-08: all 12 owl:Class declarations become entity types and all 11 owl:ObjectProperty declarations become relations with their declared rdfs:domain/rdfs:range preserved exactly. The 8 owl:DatatypeProperty declarations have NO representation here — see the _datatype_properties_note field below; that is a real coverage gap, not an oversight.
_datatype_properties_note: The source declares 8 owl:DatatypeProperty (agreementId, effectiveDate, fundName, commitmentAmount, currency, managementFee, performanceFee, lei). ADR-0007's entity_records contract stores typed MENTIONS with provenance, not per-entity attribute key/values, so a datatype property cannot be expressed as either an entity type or a relation. Consequence: amounts, dates, fee percentages, agreement identifiers, AND `lei` in a document are NOT extractable under this pack — v11 (2026-08-08) withdrew the gazetteer/external-id plane that previously captured `lei` as a partial exception, so no datatype property survives translation now. If these facts must land in the graph, the options are (a) add companion entity types (MonetaryAmount/Date/Percentage/Identifier) plus relations to carry them, or (b) extend the artifact contract with an attribute plane — (b) is an ADR-0007 change, not a pack edit.

entity_types.guidance: The overall investing relationship between an investor and an investment manager — the top-level record that ties together the parties, their governing agreement and their subscriptions.
A party that commits capital — an institution, fund-of-funds, pension scheme, family office or individual subscribing to a fund.
The firm that manages the fund and its investment programme (general partner, asset manager, adviser).
The contract governing the investment relationship — limited partnership agreement, investment management agreement, subscription agreement or similar named document.
A specific act of subscribing into a fund under the relationship — the instrument recording that an investor bought in.
The named investment vehicle being invested into (a fund, sub-fund, feeder or share class named as such).
The committed capital undertaking attached to a subscription — the named commitment obligation itself, not its numeric amount (amounts are a datatype property this pack cannot carry).
The commercial terms of an agreement — the negotiated economics clause covering fees, hurdles, carry and discounts.
A named fee schedule, fee table or fee appendix that defines how fees are calculated.
A document amending an existing agreement — amendment, restatement, addendum or variation deed.
A side letter supplementing an agreement with investor-specific terms (MFN, fee rebates, reporting or capacity rights).
The formally incorporated legal person behind a party — the registered company, partnership or trust, identified where possible by its Legal Entity Identifier (LEI).

relations.guidance: An investment relationship has an investor as one of its parties.
An investment relationship has an investment manager as its other party.
An investment relationship is governed by an agreement.
An investment relationship includes a subscription.
A subscription invests into a named fund.
A subscription carries a capital commitment.
An agreement sets out commercial terms.
Commercial terms are defined by a fee schedule.
An agreement is amended by an amendment document.
An agreement is supplemented by a side letter.
An investor is backed by a formally incorporated legal entity.
